title: Effect of resveratrol on inflammatory cytokines: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials - ScienceDirect

Accumulating evidence has described the effect of resveratrol, a natural polyphenolic compound, on biomarkers of inflammation among patients with CVDs; however, findings are controversial. Here we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effect of resveratrol supplements on TNF-α, IL-6, and CRP levels in CVDs patients.
Hence, here we tried to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis on the RCTs evaluation the effects of resveratrol supplementation on the inflammatory mediators, including interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6, IL-8, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α in a combination of pooled inflammatory diseases.
The aim of the current study was to perform a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials regarding the effect of resveratrol in decreasing the levels of inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6, IL-8, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α in a combination of inflammatory diseases.
According to trials, resveratrol is involved in the suppression of nuclear factor (NF)-κB and Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), resulting in decreased levels of inflammatory cytokines (Kang et al., 2009). Furthermore, resveratrol was shown to modulate the mRNA binding activity of KH-type splicing regulatory protein (KSRP), leading to promotion of mRNA degradation of inflammatory mediators (Bollmann et al., 2014).
